clue.text: A right tedious bod with little Mary in the garden

parts.note: a tedious person is a bore
old British slang for the stomach, from a J. M. Barrie play; a tum

explanation.surface: Someone dull is out in the garden with a small girl called Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' is a dated British euphemism for the stomach, giving TUM, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden planted with trees.

clue.text: A light weapon beloved of storytellers

definitions.text: A light weapon beloved of storytellers

parts.words: A light weapon beloved of storytellers
parts.note: read as a weapon that fires beams of light, a staple of science fiction writers rather than real armouries

explanation.surface: A handy weapon favoured by tellers of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' seems to mean not heavy, but it is the beam the weapon shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon firing a beam of energy is a stock gadget of science fiction.

clue.text: Timely word from officer on security measure

parts.note: a lock keeps a door secure

explanation.surface: An officer says something about a security precaution.
explanation.definitionFit: The word follows an hour when telling the time, so it is a word of timing.

clue.text: Give relief to printing unit manager

parts.note: an em is a unit of measure in printing

explanation.surface: A print-shop manager is told to ease the pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' suggests comfort, but here it means a raised design.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a design in relief on a surface is to stamp it up from behind.

clue.text: Saying nothing, ignoring daughter, leading to anger and offence

indicators.note: the first piece leads on to the next, placing it before
ignoring the daughter means her letter is left out of the word

explanation.surface: A silent person, snubbing a daughter, ends up furious and hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring daughter' drops D from DUMB to leave UMB, which 'leading to' puts before RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking umbrage means taking offence at a slight.

clue.text: Loud man rows on account of boundaries with neighbours

parts.note: F is forte, the musical term for loud
tiers are rows stacked one above another

explanation.surface: A noisy fellow argues over where the borders lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels but means lines, TIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Frontiers are borders between countries that sit next to each other.

clue.text: Wimbledon's oft-proclaimed benefit

definitions.meaning: the score the umpire calls at deuce in tennis, heard constantly at Wimbledon

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the tennis umpire's call after deuce and a general word for a favourable position.

clue.text: Artificial sweetener could hurt my cat, alec!

indicators.note: hurt suggests damaging and mangling, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone warns Alec that a sugar substitute might harm their pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamate is a synthetic sugar substitute, banned in some countries.

clue.text: When I finally entered into battle?

indicators.note: the letters go into the battle word, as if joining the fight
finally picks the last letter of the word entered

explanation.surface: A soldier wonders on which occasion they finally joined the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' plus the last letter of 'entered' gives ID, which goes into FRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week answers a question about time, so it can stand for a when.

clue.text: Sweet dishes providing course British can tuck into

indicators.note: tucking into means slipping inside, so one letter is put within the course word

parts.note: a syllabus is a course of study

explanation.surface: A course of study is offered where Brits can enjoy puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating, but here B tucks into SYLLABUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabubs are frothy desserts of whipped cream and wine.

clue.text: Call for some to be confined in course of virulent ailment

indicators.text: some to be confined in course of
indicators.note: some letters are held within the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some patients must be isolated during a severe illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to require or necessitate it.

clue.text: One would be a fool to wear it

definitions.text: One would be a fool to wear it

parts.words: One would be a fool to wear it
parts.note: read literally: the conical paper hat once put on a slow pupil, worn because one is a fool

explanation.surface: Putting this on would be idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says only an idiot would wear it; the cryptic sense is that the wearer is labelled as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed paper hat was put on slow schoolchildren as a punishment.

clue.text: Winner not given gold, I am injured party

indicators.note: the gold is withheld, so those letters are removed

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A champion denied the gold medal feels wronged.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldic gold; removing it from VICTOR leaves VICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is someone harmed or wronged.

clue.text: Old football manager giving Malay refs trouble

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A former coach gives referees from Malaysia a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges MALAY REFS. Sir Alf Ramsey managed England to the 1966 World Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: He managed England's football team to World Cup victory in 1966.

clue.text: Sailor with blemish kept off the rum?

parts.note: something with a blemish is stained

explanation.surface: A marked sailor stayed away from the grog.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that staying off rum is just one example of abstaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains from alcohol has abstained.

clue.text: Duller journalist made to feel good?

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A rather boring reporter is complimented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duller' looks like a description, but it is FLATTER, a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Being praised, sincerely or not, makes a person feel pleased.

clue.text: Blue-eyed boy's sulk?

definitions.meaning: a favourite, especially of a teacher

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a teacher's favourite and a fit of sullen bad temper.

clue.text: Drink up, mate!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat

explanation.surface: A toast urging a friend to finish their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink up' looks like a call to finish, but 'up' turns LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is a friend, and in British use a mate is a friend.

clue.text: Boat making stomach churn over

indicators.note: turning over means the word is flipped end to end

explanation.surface: A vessel whose motion leaves the passengers queasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a small powerful boat that tows larger ships.

clue.text: Tag Los Angeles's orchid petals

parts.note: LA is the short form of Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A label is put on flowers from California.
explanation.definitionFit: The labellum is the lip petal of an orchid, and labella is its plural.

clue.text: Not grand, but honest

definitions.meaning: a piano that stands vertically rather than a grand piano

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the vertical piano type, as opposed to a grand, and a term for a person of integrity.

clue.text: Cricket side in stage of competition

definitions.meaning: the on side of a cricket field
one round or section of a contest

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the on side of the field has this name, and a contest is split into such rounds.

clue.text: Building certified for demolition but there's no right time

indicators.note: demolishing knocks the word down so its letters are rebuilt in a new order
says these letters are missing from the word

explanation.surface: A building has been approved for pulling down, though timing is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no' removes R and T from CERTIFIED, and 'for demolition' rearranges the remaining CEIFIED.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure.

clue.text: Turn is rubbish at end of revue

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the show

explanation.surface: A performer's act is panned at the close of a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a stage act, which fits the revue, but it means spin.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to spin round an axis.

clue.text: Pretentious Greek character's two appearances

indicators.note: showing up twice means the letter is written two times

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A showy figure from Greece turns up twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi describes something affectedly fussy or showy.

clue.text: Disorder of horses very evident in foreign country

indicators.note: the letter shows up within the country

explanation.surface: An equine ailment is common abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Spavin is a swelling of a horse's hock joint that causes lameness.

clue.text: Glass paper

definitions.meaning: a newspaper, The ... being a British tabloid

explanation.definitionFit: It is a looking-glass and also the name of the British tabloid The Daily Mirror.

clue.text: See one store in the block closing early

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the shortened block
the word is closed early, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Look, a single shop in this block shuts ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese. 'closing early' removes K from BRICK, leaving BRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is his diocese, the area under his authority.

clue.text: Put into a box to be sent away, maiden wasn't well!

definitions.text: Put into a box to be sent away

parts.note: M stands for maiden, a scoreless over in cricket

explanation.surface: Posting a letter, the young woman felt poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a girl, but it is cricket's scoreless over, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a letter in a postbox sends it by post.

clue.text: Find cosy drive being disrupted

indicators.note: disrupting throws the order out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant road trip is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found.

clue.text: We hear small island is a hole

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said aloud and sounds like another

parts.note: an islet is a small island

explanation.surface: We're told a tiny island is just a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced hole for a lace or cord.

clue.text: Starters and drinks taken around good pub

indicators.note: the drinks wrap round the other letters

explanation.surface: Appetisers and drinks are had at a decent pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' looks like first courses, which fits the pub, but means novices.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginners are those just starting out.
